To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

strenuous exercise causes an increase in the concentration of respiratory enzyme proteins and in the total protein content of mitochondria in muscle, and that these changes are associated with an increase in aerobic work capability.
the mitochondrial respiratory chain is up regulated in response to exercise training.

the capacity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain in rat skeletal muscle increases in response to strenuous exercise, and that this increase in capacity is due to an increase both in the amount of cytochrome and in the total amount of protein in the mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise on the biochemical properties of skeletal muscle.
the biochemical adaptations that take place in muscle as a result of exercise training.
the biochemical adaptations of muscle to exercise, and with the possible use of exercise as a tool for studying the synthesis of mitochondrial proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise increases oxidative capacity in muscle.

exercise increases the capacity of the muscle mitochondria to oxidize pyrvvate and that this increase is due to an increase both in the concentration of respiratory enzyme proteins and in the total protein content of muscle mitochondria.

strenuous exercise causes an increase in the capacity of muscle to oxidize carbohydrate substrates, and that the increased capacity for oxidative phosphorylation is due to an increase of the concentration of respiratory enzyme protein in the mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increase in respiratory capacity in the trained animals is due to an increase both in the number of mitochondria and in the concentration of the respiratory enzymes.
exercise can increase the number of mitochondria and the amount of cytochrome in the mitochondria, thus increasing the capacity of the muscle to use oxygen.
we have found that the mitochondrial fraction from muscle of rats subjected to a 6-week program of treadmill running has a higher respiratory capacity than that of control animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondria in the muscles of rats that exercised regularly had a higher capacity to oxidize pyridine nucleotides and to produce ATP.
the mitochondrial respiratory chain is the most adaptable part of the cell to changes in workload and that it is a major determinant of the ability of cells to produce energy.
exercise is an important factor in the development of the mitochondrial system in the muscle cell.
